title: What If You Fell Into Icy Water? The First Minute Decides

scenes.text: What if you fell into icy water? The cold isn't what gets you first.
scenes.keywords: person falling into lake icy water

scenes.text: Within seconds, cold shock triggers an involuntary gasp that you can't stop.
Experts give you about one minute to get your breathing under control. Float on your back and let it pass.
scenes.keywords: person floating on back in water

scenes.text: By about ten minutes, the muscles in your arms and legs stop working well. Swimming for shore becomes nearly impossible.
Hypothermia is slower. You may have roughly an hour before you lose consciousness.
That's the one, ten, one rule: one minute, ten minutes, one hour. Most of the fight is won in the first sixty seconds.

description:
What if you fell into icy water?
Cold shock hits in seconds, muscles fail around ten minutes, and consciousness can go around an hour. Experts call it the 1-10-1 rule.
